petitionNoChildren.name: Petition for Dissolution of Marriage (No Children)

petitionWithChildren.name: Petition for Dissolution of Marriage (With Children)

residencyRequirements.description: One or both spouses must be Illinois residents for 90 days. Residency can be established before filing OR before judgment.

separationPresumption.description: If parties have lived separate and apart for 6 continuous months, irreconcilable differences are presumed. Both parties may waive the 6-month period by written stipulation.

waitingPeriod.description: Illinois has no mandatory waiting period, but residency requirement must be met before judgment. If parties have not been separated for 6 months, they must affirmatively establish irreconcilable differences; 6 months separation creates a rebuttable presumption.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences have caused the irretrievable breakdown of the marriage
noFault.notes: This is the ONLY ground for dissolution in Illinois as of January 1, 2016

groundsForDissolution.note: Illinois eliminated all fault-based grounds effective January 1, 2016

formattingRequirements.notes: Must use Statewide Approved Standardized Forms - all Illinois Circuit Courts must accept these forms

options: Other county by written motion and hearing

legalCitations.description: Illinois Marriage and Dissolution of Marriage Act

filingFees.notes: Varies by county. Cook County charges $388 for a Petition for Dissolution of Marriage (respondent appearance fee is $251). Other counties may be lower. Fee waiver available for qualifying individuals under 735 ILCS 5/5-105.

formula.calculation: (33.33% of payor's net income) - (25% of payee's net income)
formula.cap: Combined maintenance and payee's net income cannot exceed 40% of combined net income
formula.incomeThreshold: Formula applies only when combined gross income is under $500,000; above that threshold, the court uses discretionary statutory factors

examples: 20+ years: Indefinite or equal to marriage length

propertyDivision.description: Illinois is an equitable distribution state. Marital property is divided in just proportions (not necessarily equal).
factors: Contribution of each party to acquisition of marital property
Value of property set apart to each spouse
Relevant economic circumstances of each spouse
Age, health, station, occupation, income, skills, employability of each party
Whether award is in lieu of or in addition to maintenance
Reasonable opportunity for future acquisition of assets
